# Plan 4 — Scenario Campaign Library

**Wave:** 1 of 4
**Status:** DRAFT — bootstrap and campaign authority audit required
**Pass:** 28 (planning continues)
**Target:** 200,000 substantive words across iterative passes
**Scope:** route-verified campaign episodes through existing start, quest, and feature surfaces

## Field 01 — Player experience and core loop

The player chooses a clear starting situation, understands its special constraints before committing, and plays an authored short or long campaign with a defined objective and several valid outcomes. A scenario should create a different strategic opening, not simply apply a difficulty label or rename an existing quest.

The initial library aims for six starts across different play styles: a shelter with unreliable water, a damaged route and limited transport, an isolated medical demand, a failed relay, an exposed outpost, and a low-supply industrial site. These are hypotheses; each must be mapped to existing start-state and campaign owners before authoring.

The live source includes SliceScenario and TradeScreenScenarios, so a general scenario framework cannot be presumed missing. Determine what those types own, whether they are production-facing, and whether another campaign start authority exists. If there is a current owner, extend it. Do not introduce a new campaign simulator or bypass the existing game bootstrap.

## Field 02 — Scenario rules and campaign mechanics

Each scenario has a fixed, documented starting snapshot, one primary objective, optional objectives, a day or event window, and consequence rules. Objectives refer to current gameplay facts: restore a service, reach a site, resolve an active threat, stabilize the population, or make a difficult trade. The scenario must not mutate unrelated hidden state or grant arbitrary resources.

Scenario rules can configure starting inventories, known locations, initial trust, active hazards, and optional restrictions only through approved setup seams. Difficulty remains owned by the canonical difficulty system. A scenario can recommend a preset or describe its intended pressure, but it must not set a second scalar or silently overwrite player settings.

Objective resolution uses the current quest/campaign event producers. All branching must have an explicit producer, consumer, success path, failure path, cancellation behavior, and restored-state behavior. Scenario completion should not end the whole campaign unless the existing endgame owner says it does.

## Field 03 — Scenario data and high-volume content

Proposed first catalogue: 6 starts, 18 primary objectives, 24 optional objectives, 36 event beats, 30 briefing fragments, 24 consequence records, and 12 ending summaries. Expand toward 12 starts only after each initial scenario proves distinct play and successful save/restore.

Fields should include scenario ID, schema version, display title, briefing key, start profile reference, allowed difficulty range, objective IDs, optional objective IDs, validity conditions, event schedule, completion conditions, failure conditions, outcome mappings, and accessibility notes. Data must reference current catalog IDs and use validators. Any scenario-only start change must have a deterministic and auditable owner.

Keep text data separate from mechanics. Authored prose may explain the situation, but objective reachability is expressed in validated fields and verified against runtime facts.

## Field 04 — Main storylines

**Seven Days at Coldwater** begins with a marginal water source and a forecast that closes one route. The player chooses between securing the pump, relocating water, or seeking help from a neighboring group. Its endings reflect actual water, trust, and access state.

**The Relay That Answered** begins after an unexpected signal at a damaged relay. The player can investigate the location, secure power, or prioritize the human request that arrived. The campaign uses current communications, map, and faction owners; it does not duplicate radio transmission content recently sealed in Wave 40.

**A Place for the Clinic** begins with an outpost asking for medical support while the shelter has a competing crisis. The player chooses whether to send a qualified team, prepare the receiving site, or delay and negotiate a local alternative. It may reuse Plan 2’s mobile outreach content only after that plan’s authority audit and content schema are complete.

**The Last Kilowatt** begins with a power fault in an industrial site and a small reserve. The player must decide what to keep online, who will inspect the damaged equipment, and whether to promise a delivery that may not arrive. The scenario relies on existing power and economy owners, not new meters.

## Field 05 — Side quests and optional objectives

Each start should have 4–6 optional activities that change preparation or understanding: find a maintenance ledger; compare two reports; identify a safe route; persuade a worker to join a shift; return a borrowed item; inspect a water sample; negotiate access; document a hazard; restore a small utility; recover a missing radio part; deliver medicine; evacuate a noncombatant; preserve a record; recruit a local guide; and close an unresolved complaint.

Optional objectives are genuinely optional: failure cannot make the primary objective impossible unless that failure is the scenario’s stated challenge. The UI should state whether an objective is time-sensitive, repeatable, mutually exclusive, or only informational.

Quest text should be concise and action-oriented. Repeated system prose belongs in reusable localization-ready templates with named variables and safe fallbacks. Avoid generating large amounts of near-identical branching prose to hit a volume target.

## Field 06 — Integration and existing-plan unblocking

The first dependency is the currently active XP difficulty work. Scenario selection must consume the resulting canonical settings API after its owner closes the claim; do not edit active difficulty paths or create local difficulty state. The plan also depends on current campaign bootstrap, save metadata, quest runtime, location identity, and endgame owners.

Before proposing a general scenario catalog, compare SliceScenario and other start profiles with the exact plans in the register. Resolve any overlap as an extension or closeout of that plan. The scenario library cannot unblock held plans by silently satisfying their premise; accepted HOLD entries still need their recorded conditions and signature.

Create an exact path list and ownership claim before implementation. If a new start schema or save field needs a decision, request it through the proper foreman route. This plan owns no live integration queue, shared ledger, or current active implementation path.

## Field 07 — UI scaffolding

The scenario browser shows start condition, intended duration, key pressures, content prerequisites, accessibility notes, and whether the profile is compatible with current campaign settings. A preview provides the opening briefing and explains any irreversible choices. The confirmation view states what starting a scenario will replace or create according to the existing save contract.

The scenario page must be reachable through a real menu route and must not be an isolated prototype panel. The play button constructs the approved scenario through the canonical bootstrap and returns a truthful result. Invalid catalog or missing owner status should produce a recoverable error rather than starting a partial campaign.

After start, a compact objective panel shows the primary objective, available optional objectives, and actual progress facts. The same facts remain accessible from the campaign’s current objective owner.

## Field 08 — UX, accessibility, and fair challenge

Scenario selection must be fully navigable by keyboard and controller. Focus order follows title → description → pressures → objectives → start. Use readable contrast and textual labels for difficulty and danger; avoid relying on red/green. Ensure long descriptions scroll without hiding the confirmation action.

The briefing communicates known facts separately from uncertainty. Challenge starts cannot hide a critical restriction in flavor prose. Settings compatibility is explicit, and the player can return to the browser without losing their existing campaign.

The first-run experience should teach one mechanic at a time through the existing onboarding and help authorities. Do not block a new campaign behind a tutorial panel that is already dismissed or inaccessible.

## Field 09 — Performance and replayability

Measure startup construction, catalog load, save creation, and first-day simulation across 1, 6, and 12 scenario definitions using the existing performance workload harness. Scenario selection should not load every narrative payload or recompute all world data if a small metadata view is sufficient.

Same scenario plus same seed and settings must produce the same initial state and deterministic outcomes. Stable ordering is required for initial inventory, objectives, starting locations, and event scheduling. Replay comparison should exclude presentation-only timestamps but include authoritative state.

Balancing compares players with different difficulty presets and optional accessibility settings. Scenario-specific goals must remain possible across the supported range; where a preset materially changes feasibility, the preview says so. Avoid special-case logic that weakens global difficulty contracts.

## Field 10 — Persistence, verification, and rollout

The save contract identifies scenario ID, schema version, seed, chosen settings, and objective state in the approved campaign envelope. No scenario should keep a second copy of survivor, inventory, route, hazard, or faction state. Restoring a scenario must not replay its opening reward, reset its objective, or reroll its initial conditions.

Proposed focused acceptance covers catalog validation, every start profile, start-state parity, difficulty compatibility, unreachable objective detection, success/failure/cancel paths, deterministic paired starts, save round-trip, old-save compatibility, UI route, controller focus, accessibility, and bounded startup cost. Tests are proposed, not run.

Roll out one short scenario first, then two mechanically distinct starts, then the full library. Keep legacy campaign start unaffected. Promote only after a full bootstrap and save-owner audit, current XP work is closed, and no existing plan owns the same scenario contract.

## Pass 1 closeout

This candidate is least certain of the four: the repository has specialized scenario types and active difficulty work. It must pass the strictest collision and authority review. If no genuinely missing player-facing capability remains, repurpose this plan as a scenario content and route-completion package rather than adding a new framework.

## Pass 2 — Scenario matrix and campaign scaffolding

### Field 01 supplement — scenario selection as a player promise

A scenario preview is a contract. It tells the player what kind of pressure they are choosing, what they already know, how long the authored arc is expected to run, which options are supported, and what counts as resolution. The selected scenario should shape early decisions through real state, not through a hidden difficulty multiplier or scripted failure.

Every start can be played in the ordinary campaign loop. Scenario objectives should not require the player to guess an undisclosed key or follow one exact dialogue path. The player can pause, inspect, decline an optional objective, and return to the main goal. A short scenario can conclude with an authored summary while leaving the ordinary save and endgame owners in charge of what happens next.

The central design test is replay value: does this start create a different first week because the player has different information, relationships, routes, or material constraints? If its only difference is a larger resource penalty, it is a difficulty preset and belongs with the existing difficulty owner.

### Field 02 supplement — scenario grammar and safe start rules

Scenario definitions should be declarative and constrained. A valid profile references existing survivor, item, location, weather, faction, and objective IDs. It may describe which existing state to initialize, but it cannot embed an alternate copy of those systems. Start creation is transactional: either all required starting facts resolve and the campaign starts, or the user receives a clear error and no half-created save.

Possible scenario dimensions include:

- Starting knowledge: known route, incomplete map, disputed report, or verified warning.
- Starting relationships: an existing obligation, low trust, or a prior unresolved agreement.
- Material constraint: a smaller or specialized stock profile using current inventory definitions.
- Time pressure: a published deadline or weather window from canonical campaign time.
- Access constraint: a real location access state accepted by the map/faction owner.
- Objective structure: one primary goal with optional goals that are clearly labeled.
- Failure shape: a bounded consequence with a recovery path, not an invisible instant loss.

Rules are validated before the player can start. Each initializer has an explicit owner API, order, idempotency key, and failure result. The scenario ID and seed are immutable for that run. Restarting creates a new campaign through the current bootstrap rather than mutating a live campaign in place.

### Field 03 supplement — content matrix for six candidate starts

| Candidate | Opening constraint | Primary objective | Optional objectives | Distinct replay axis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seven Days at Coldwater | Water access is uncertain; one route may close | Establish a safe short-term water plan | Verify two sources; arrange a shared allocation | Evidence versus immediate repair |
| The Relay That Answered | A damaged relay has an incoming request | Restore or intentionally defer service | Verify the sender; preserve the old access rule | Information trust |
| A Place for the Clinic | Remote medical demand conflicts with shelter readiness | Create a viable care response | Confirm demand; prepare a receiving site | Staff and consent |
| The Last Kilowatt | Industrial power is unstable and stock is limited | Protect one essential service | Inspect a fault; negotiate a delivery | Repair versus triage |
| North Watch, No Roster | An outpost has a gap in staffing records | Reconcile actual duty and supply facts | Find the missing log; obtain local consent | Known people, unknown duty |
| Grain in the Ash | A food store remains sealed after a contamination warning | Make a safe decision about stock | Verify the warning; recover a sample | Caution versus waste |

These are proposed scenario titles, not confirmed canon. Plan 1–3 may share a setting or a character only after the canon registry and existing expansion context have been checked. Scenario crossovers should be optional and driven by persisted facts, not by assuming every player completed all starts.

For the first content tranche, author 6 primary objective graphs, 24 optional objectives, 36 event beats, 24 debrief outcomes, 18 opening reports, 24 follow-up callbacks, and 12 difficulty compatibility notes. Every row must be traceable to a consumer.

### Field 04 supplement — authored scenario arcs

Each scenario can use a consistent ten-beat template while keeping the actual pressure distinct.

**Seven Days at Coldwater:** an incomplete source report; inspection of a pump and a hand-drawn level mark; a conflicting household account; a route forecast that narrows the choice; negotiation over shared draw; discovery of a ledger kept outside the official log; a choice between immediate output and verified repair; an operational result sent to the water owner; a callback after the water level changes; and a closeout showing who can rely on the source.

**The Relay That Answered:** an unscheduled signal; a maintenance discrepancy; corroboration from a physically recovered note; a dispute over access; a power shortage; an incoming request that cannot be fully verified; a choice to restore shared service, restrict it, or wait; a real relay/access result; a delayed message reflecting the rule; and a persistent local record.

**A Place for the Clinic:** a remote request; route and staffing review; conflicting medical facts; consent conversation; access negotiation; a weather interruption; a decision to send, prepare locally, or defer; medical and expedition results; a follow-up from the receiving site; and a closeout that names what is still unknown.

**The Last Kilowatt:** an unstable reading; comparison to a past maintenance slip; disagreement over the load priority; a shortage of a specific part; a worker identifies a safe inspection window; a competing delivery promise; a choice to reduce load, repair, or relocate work; a power owner result; a delayed consequence in production or trust; and a documented operating limit.

This shared structure helps authors verify branch completeness. It must not make every scenario sound alike. Briefings, people, objective graphs, and consequences should come from each specific system.

### Field 05 supplement — objective quality and side-quest volume

An objective is useful when it adds a decision, a source of evidence, or a consequence. It should not be counted as new content merely because its text differs. Candidate optional objectives include: recover a service ledger; verify a conflicting location name; ask permission before entering; secure a route window; recruit a qualified worker; reduce an item loss; identify a stale report; record who authorized a repair; return a borrowed tool; preserve a disputed message; complete an inspection; obtain informed consent; arrange a safe fallback; disclose an uncertainty; and revisit a site after a day advances.

Each scenario should include at least four optional objectives, including one investigation, one logistics choice, one relationship/access choice, and one recovery opportunity. At least one can be missed without invalidating the primary objective. Mutually exclusive objectives state their conflict before the player commits.

The debrief distinguishes objective success, objective failure, and unresolved facts. Do not label a scenario a failure solely because an optional objective was missed. The result summary cites authoritative facts and avoids hidden composite scores.

### Field 06 supplement — bootstrap, authority, and plan collision matrix

| Concern | Reuse or inspect | Hard stop |
|---|---|---|
| Starting game state | Existing campaign bootstrap and scenario adapters | No second bootstrap path |
| Difficulty | Canonical DifficultySettingsSystem after XP W1 closes | No local scalar or silent override |
| Objective progression | Existing quest and campaign event owners | No parallel quest state |
| Locations and route access | Current map and expedition contracts | No scenario-only duplicate geography |
| Faction relations | Current faction/standing owner | No invented faction IDs or shadow trust |
| Save identity | Current campaign/save envelope | No independent scenario save file without a decision |
| User settings and focus | Current settings/input/UI contracts | No scenario-only preference store |

The supplied AGENTS queue lists XP work as active. The live ledger also contains a newer batch state than some supplied queue notes. Confirm the actual owner and closeout before touching any affected file. Compare all candidate starts against the plan register and relevant short plan indexes. If a prior plan already owns a start profile or scenario route, merge the content into that workstream.

### Fields 07–08 supplement — browser behavior and accessible challenge

The browser has three levels: scenario list, scenario detail, and start confirmation. The list allows comparison without selecting a start. Detail includes the full opening briefing, known pressures, prerequisites, expected duration band, and supported settings. Confirmation summarizes the exact initialized profile and asks whether the player wants a fresh run under the current save contract.

Empty, invalid, or incompatible catalog states are explicit. The player can cancel without replacing a save. The starting action remains disabled until all profile references validate. A canceled start creates no hidden seed record or partial inventory.

Use a consistent focus order, clear back behavior, controller support, readable contrast, and text labels for all scenario pressure icons. Ensure long briefing text does not push the start control below an unreachable scroll region. Give the user control over motion effects through current settings. Challenge labels communicate conditions rather than ranking players.

### Fields 09–10 supplement — startup cost, determinism, and release matrix

The performance matrix measures metadata browsing, first preview, campaign initialization, first-day tick, and save capture for 1, 6, and 12 scenarios. Only the selected scenario’s full event payload should load if the existing catalog pipeline supports lazy access; do not add a cache until measurements show the need. The startup path should never validate every large prose bundle synchronously on every panel open.

The determinism matrix repeats each scenario with fixed seed and identical settings, then compares canonical initial state and a bounded sequence of daily outcomes. Restart semantics are tested separately from load semantics. Load resumes the same scenario; restart creates a new campaign; opening the scenario browser changes no campaign state.

Release the scenario library in three steps: first one start that exercises existing owners with no new save state; second two starts with distinct constraint types; third the remaining content only after route, save, and accessibility review. Promotion requires source evidence that the capability is missing or incomplete, a signed owner decision for any new initialization state, a distinct-content review, and a successful end-to-end acceptance package. If that evidence fails, keep the content as a routed short campaign under the current owner and remove the proposed framework.

## Pass 3 — Scenario profile grammar and launchable content slice

### Field 01 expansion — a scenario must make a clear promise

The first scenario should be selected by a reviewer who can describe its promise in one sentence: which existing systems will be under pressure, what kind of choice the player will face, and what information will remain uncertain. Its briefing then demonstrates that promise in play. A scenario is not a difficulty preset with a title; it changes the opening facts and objective context enough to create a distinct first hour while preserving the same canonical authorities.

The candidate called Seven Days at Coldwater can serve as an initial profile only if water access, route, and report uncertainty form a genuinely different opening from the main campaign. The first action is to check a source or begin a conservative allocation. The first milestone is an owner-confirmed service or access result. The slice closes with a debrief that names whether the water is available, restricted, or still uncertain and gives the player one concrete next task.

Scenario selection must not overwrite an existing campaign. Preview, confirmation, failed validation, and cancellation all leave current save identity and state intact. Start either creates a complete initialized campaign or reports the exact unmet profile reference.

### Field 02 expansion — staged initialization and rollback

Proposed start transaction stages are profile validation, referenced-catalog validation, save-slot selection, seed acceptance, owner-by-owner initialization, initial receipt collection, and campaign activation. Each stage needs an idempotency key or another current mechanism that prevents partial replay. If initialization fails, the system must discard the staged result or roll it back using existing save ownership.

The profile may request initial conditions through owner commands, such as starting location, known reports, relationship facts, or inventory scenario presets. It may not directly fill private system fields or reconstruct subsystem objects. The selected profile ID, profile revision, seed, and supported settings should be visible in the campaign summary if the current save envelope has a place for them. New save fields require a signed decision and migration plan.

### Field 03 expansion — profile cards and objective map

The six current candidates should each be made into a concise, comparable card:

| Profile | Opening fact to verify | First objective receipt | Optional objective categories |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seven Days at Coldwater | Is either water source reliable? | Accepted allocation or inspection | Investigation, access, logistics, recovery |
| The Relay That Answered | Who sent the signal and when? | Confirmed message or service result | Evidence, shared access, repair, callback |
| A Place for the Clinic | What care is requested and by whom? | Medical/route owner result | Consent, staff, supplies, receiving site |
| The Last Kilowatt | Which load is unstable and why? | Power owner status | Inspection, repair, trade, safe reduction |
| North Watch, No Roster | Which duty facts are current? | Verified assignment or site report | Contact, missing record, supply, return |
| Grain in the Ash | Which stock is affected by the warning? | Food owner inspection or disposition | Evidence, storage, access, waste reduction |

Each profile then lists a short objective graph using typed prerequisites, action references, and result facts. Objectives can be optional, alternative, or terminal. Use an explicit cancellation edge for objectives invalidated by a player decision. Do not create a separate mission scripting language when the current quest graph supports the same requirement.

### Field 04 expansion — story structure without repeated plots

Give each scenario a distinct source of uncertainty and a distinct social cost. Coldwater has conflicting measurements and competing water needs; the Relay begins with an unknown sender and access rules; the Clinic has uncertain demand and consent; the Last Kilowatt concerns safe allocation of unstable power; North Watch concerns the reliability of records and the limits of duty; Grain in the Ash concerns whether a precaution is justified and how safely to handle stock.

The authoring card for every beat records speaker role, current knowledge, source of the information, action unlocked, possible contradiction, and follow-up trigger. Characters never deliver facts they could not know. A missed objective changes the available evidence or outcome but does not erase the primary path without a clear warning. Every scenario includes a low-conflict route, a resource-constrained route, and an uncertainty-preserving route so replay choices are systemic rather than merely different dialogue.

### Field 05 expansion — optional objective packets

Seed the planned side-objective volume with sixteen reusable action packets:

| Packet | Applies to | Mechanical purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Compare two dated reports | All profiles | Establish source and confidence |
| Recover the missing receipt | Water, power, food | Reconcile a prior transaction |
| Ask a local custodian | Relay, outpost | Confirm consent and access |
| Inspect a return route | Clinic, relay | Reveal route status |
| Preserve a disputed message | Relay, roster | Record uncertainty and provenance |
| Verify the receiving site | Clinic, water | Prevent unsupported completion |
| Trace a damaged item | Power, food | Locate a valid replacement |
| Report a safe alternative | All profiles | Keep a recovery path open |
| Request a second inspection | Water, power, food | Distinguish claim from confirmation |
| Schedule a shared work window | Relay, outpost | Resolve access without a hidden score |
| Find a previous agreement | Water, clinic | Reopen a real obligation |
| Close an unreachable request | All profiles | Preserve an honest terminal path |
| Return borrowed equipment | All profiles | Complete an inventory obligation |
| Publish a corrected notice | Relay, roster | Update knowledge through its owner |
| Revisit after a day advances | All profiles | Test persistence and callback |
| Document an unresolved fact | All profiles | Preserve uncertainty as a valid result |

Reusability means the same player action can support several scenarios; it does not mean identical text or automatic completion. Each use needs scenario-specific context and a distinct source reference.

### Field 06 expansion — plan fit and content collision protocol

For each proposed profile, record related plans by exact ID and current status, including accepted, partial, active, blocked, and retired work. The comparison needs a short content fingerprint: opening premise, unique characters, locations, objective verbs, system authority, and ending facts. If two plans share a premise, fold the smaller content into the correct current owner or change the scenario focus before implementation.

The scenario library can unblock other plans by supplying a bounded route through existing systems, a visible content consumer, a missing initial producer, or a closeout callback. The handoff must cite evidence and name the file owner; the scenario profile alone is not authority to implement a blocked architecture choice. Verify all difficulty consumers against the live XP work before defining scenario modifiers.

### Field 07 expansion — browser and new-campaign path

The browser list provides a card title, premise, pressure tags, supported settings, estimated commitment band if evidence exists, and a clear resume/start distinction. Scenario details show opening facts, the first objective, optional objective categories, known prerequisites, and what the profile initializes. They must not reveal future narrative outcomes as though they were guaranteed.

The start confirmation repeats the profile, seed behavior, settings, and destination save slot. If the current campaign occupies the target slot, the user must choose an available slot or return; no destructive replacement is implied by a generic Start label. Validation errors identify a missing referenced ID in a human-readable form and offer a safe way back to the list.

### Field 08 expansion — fair challenge and comprehension review

Challenge comes from constrained resources, partial information, and competing valid needs. It should not depend on hidden modifiers, random death at launch, inaccessible prerequisites, or descriptions that promise a result the owners cannot deliver. Before an irreversible scenario decision, show what the player knows, what remains uncertain, and which commitment will be made.

Review a scenario with first-time readers using a short comprehension sheet: can they identify the primary objective; distinguish optional goals; tell which reports are uncertain; explain what start will change; and find a way to pause or leave? The review measures wording and navigation, not whether the player chose the author’s preferred moral outcome.

### Field 09 expansion — replay and workload envelope

Replay differences should come from stable seed-controlled inputs or explicitly selected starting facts. The same seed, profile revision, and settings must produce the same canonical initial state. User-facing text may vary only through deterministic authored variants. Loading the active campaign resumes; starting again creates a separate campaign under the current save rules.

Measure the list with 1, 6, 12, and 24 profile cards; objective previews with short and long graphs; missing references; and large localized briefing text. Measure first preview, first start, campaign capture, resume, and restart separately. If long prose delays the browser, use the current content loading method; do not add a parallel catalog cache without profiling.

### Field 10 expansion — review packet for one launchable profile

A profile is implementation-ready only with its source-premise evidence, content fingerprint, objective graph, initializer owner calls, save behavior, rollback result, visible launch path, complete cancellation behavior, accessibility review, and focused verification plan. Its acceptance walk should start from the scenario list, preview the profile, cancel once, start successfully, inspect the resulting initial state, save, load, and confirm that browsing or retrying did not mutate the active run.

The first launch package should contain one profile and enough optional objectives to prove branching. Add the remaining profiles only after the first has a successful end-to-end route and no duplicate system authority. If no new scenario-selection capability is missing, use the existing campaign and quest owners to author distinct content there and retire the framework proposal.

## Pass 4 — Scenario content bible and campaign release tranche

### Field 01 expansion — start-state identity and replay value

Each scenario profile needs a recognizable opening state and a different first decision. Replay value should come from the state the player begins with, the evidence they can verify, and the commitments they can make, rather than a large set of random modifiers. A new run can vary a bounded and documented input, but the scenario must still tell the player what kind of challenge they selected.

The first content comparison should ask whether each profile teaches a different system relationship: Coldwater teaches evidence and allocation; The Relay That Answered teaches message provenance and access; A Place for the Clinic teaches consent and field logistics; The Last Kilowatt teaches safe service prioritization; North Watch teaches record reconciliation and work assignment; Grain in the Ash teaches evidence-based handling of uncertain stock. If two profiles produce the same first decision and result, revise their opening or combine them.

### Field 02 expansion — profile manifest fields

Before a profile becomes catalog data, its manifest proposal should list: stable candidate ID; content revision; title and briefing keys; opening location reference; initial report references; objective graph reference; owner initialization requests; allowed difficulty and accessibility settings; expected duration band if measured; required catalog versions; seed use; save identity behavior; and cancellation/rollback contract.

Each owner initialization request names the current public command and prerequisite facts. The start operation validates all references before making any mutation. It records accepted receipts in the current campaign envelope if that envelope supports them. A failed request prevents campaign activation and returns the save to its pre-start state. Do not create compatibility values that silently alter current difficulty, XP, or save behavior.

### Field 03 expansion — profile setup cards

Extend the six scenario cards with a small setup and opening-event sequence:

| Profile | Initial setup request | First playable choice | First result surfaced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seven Days at Coldwater | Known water site and two reports of different age | Verify a source or set a conservative limit | Water/access authority confirms a source state |
| The Relay That Answered | Existing relay, dated signal, and uncertain sender | Trace provenance or restore limited service | Communications authority reports signal/service |
| A Place for the Clinic | Named request and a known receiving location | Ask for clarification or prepare a visit | Medical/expedition owners report readiness/result |
| The Last Kilowatt | Existing power load and a maintenance note | Inspect or reduce one supported load | Power owner reports service condition |
| North Watch, No Roster | Existing outpost and conflicting duty records | Reconcile a roster fact or inspect the site | Work/outpost owner reports verified staffing |
| Grain in the Ash | Existing stock and a dated warning | Hold stock for inspection or seek another source | Food owner reports accepted disposition |

The opening sequence must not create new canonical people or items merely for a scenario. Where an existing catalog has no suitable record, list the desired content row for a later content package and keep the profile disabled.

### Field 04 expansion — six campaign threads

Develop the profile stories as threads that can be completed in flexible order:

| Thread | Middle turn | Late turn | Persistent question |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coldwater allocation | A second measurement conflicts with the first | A receiving group reports whether the limit held | Who can verify shared use? |
| Relay provenance | A sender is recognized but cannot be fully authenticated | A delayed reply challenges the access rule | How much uncertainty is acceptable for service? |
| Clinic visit | The destination confirms a different need than the request implied | A return contact asks what information may be shared | What does care mean when travel or consent fails? |
| Kilowatt triage | The stable reading depends on which load is active | A maintenance worker returns with a corrected diagnosis | Who sets the safe operating limit? |
| North Watch records | Two trustworthy people kept different kinds of records | A later duty handoff tests the chosen roster rule | What should a record prove? |
| Grain warning | An inspection weakens or confirms one part of the warning | The next delivery reveals the cost of holding or releasing stock | How can caution avoid becoming waste? |

Each thread includes an opening, two middle beats, a commitment, a result, and a callback. Branches should depend on documented facts and owner receipts, with at least one route that keeps uncertainty unresolved. The player can finish the scenario’s primary objective without resolving every human disagreement.

### Field 05 expansion — side-objective packs by profile

Build four side objectives for every profile, for a first batch of 24:

| Profile | Investigation | Logistics | Access or relationship | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coldwater | Date two measurements | Find a valid container | Request a shared draw window | Recheck after a day |
| Relay | Compare message timestamps | Recover a service part | Ask the custodian to set access | Send a verified reply |
| Clinic | Clarify request source | Pack and return a case | Ask the recipient what may be shared | Arrange a new visit window |
| Kilowatt | Inspect the maintenance note | Source an accepted replacement | Agree on a temporary load rule | Confirm stable operation |
| North Watch | Compare duty records | Return a borrowed tool | Ask who may approve a roster | Check the next shift |
| Grain | Trace the warning label | Move stock to safe storage | Explain a hold to the recipient | Reopen or close the inspection |

Each objective produces a specific owner fact, a quest result, or a documented unresolved status. Side objectives may change what evidence the player receives, but they never add hidden scenario score or erase a failed primary objective.

### Field 06 expansion — scenario-to-plan unblocking map

Create a plan fit sheet for every profile listing its system owners, relevant accepted plans, active and partial plans, current decision blocks, exact content contribution, and whether that contribution can close an existing acceptance criterion. Candidate contributions include an opening event that makes a system reachable, a scenario route that exercises persistence, a missing UI consumer, a distinct outcome callback, or a bounded data-authority row.

Do not call an item an unblock until the named plan owner accepts the handoff and the integration ledger records the package. Do not use scenario writing to revive retired architecture or to bypass an XP, save, or difficulty decision. If one profile depends on another new Wave 1 system, mark it as later content and do not make it part of the first scenario release.

### Field 07 expansion — browser states and comparison

Provide list states for available, completed, currently active, locked by a missing catalog reference, and temporarily disabled during validation. The comparison view exposes opening premise, first decision, systems involved, accessibility support, measured time band, and how the run is stored. Completed profiles can be replayed only through the current save-slot contract.

The preview has three sections: What is already known; What is uncertain; What the player can affect. The screen avoids spoiler text while still naming resource or relationship pressures. A profile can be bookmarked or compared only if those actions use existing settings and do not alter campaign state.

### Field 08 expansion — settings and player agency

Difficulty, text size, contrast, controller mapping, and motion settings come from existing preferences. The scenario may declare which settings it supports, but it cannot silently change them. If the player starts with a condition that creates a one-way loss, the confirmation describes it. If the player can recover, the first recovery path is discoverable before the loss becomes irreversible.

Tutorial prompts should be triggered by the first relevant action, dismissible, and recorded through the current guidance preference. The scenario should not force a tutorial for a system the player has already learned. A player who closes the browser returns to the same campaign surface without losing a selection or changing a seed.

### Field 09 expansion — profile compatibility and telemetry-free diagnostics

Version profile content independently from save schema. On load, a campaign retains its authored profile revision or follows an explicit migration path; it must not silently substitute a newer objective graph. A removed profile can remain loadable through the current save migration owner or be marked as unavailable for new starts while preserving its active campaign.

Diagnostics should report validation stages, missing references, rejected owner initialization, duration measurements, and objective completion receipts using existing local diagnostics. Do not add a network telemetry dependency. Profile sizes and objective graph complexity are measured at 1, 6, 12, and 24 catalog entries, with large text assets handled through current loading contracts.

### Field 10 expansion — release package and completion evidence

Package A contains one profile, its opening objective, four side objectives, one callback, start cancellation, and save/load acceptance. Package B adds two profiles that use distinct owner combinations. Package C expands to all six profiles only after overlap and comprehension review. Each package lists evidence and owners rather than treating a large catalog count as acceptance.

The release report captures profile IDs, owner calls, save behavior, unresolved decisions, content rows accepted or deferred, accessibility findings, and a reader’s understanding of the first decision. A scenario is complete when it offers a distinct playable start, a truthful result, and at least one persistent callback through existing owners. If those can be delivered through the current campaign, keep the work as a content pack and close the framework proposal.

## Pass 5 — Objective graph workbook and scenario-specific content

### Field 01 expansion — scope of one scenario run

A scenario run is a curated starting condition, a primary objective, optional objectives, and a sequence of authored events that make existing game systems interact in a particular order. It is not a separate simulation. The scenario library’s value is strongest where the normal campaign exposes the same systems over a longer period but does not guarantee that players will meet the intended combination early.

Every profile should answer these practical questions: What can the player do in the first ten minutes? Which current owner will report the first result? What fact will become clearer after that result? Which follow-up remains optional? What still works if the player declines the central request? If these answers match an existing quest chain, add content to that chain instead of adding another starting framework.

### Field 02 expansion — objective graph contract

An objective node should describe a trigger, prerequisites, player action, result owner, completion evidence, failure or cancellation condition, and optional next nodes. The graph distinguishes three completion classes: owner-confirmed action; evidence collected; and narrative decision recorded. One objective may require more than one class, but the panel must show which remains.

| Node type | Example condition | Completion proof |
|---|---|---|
| Observe | Inspect an existing report or location | Source reference and timestamp |
| Verify | Compare independent evidence | Accepted confidence or dispute result |
| Commit | Dispatch, reserve, assign, or authorize | Owner transaction receipt |
| Respond | Complete the current owner action | Owner state-change receipt |
| Decide | Select an offered branch | Scenario/quest choice fact |
| Return | Visit again after a prerequisite | Arrival and callback receipt |
| Close | Resolve or intentionally defer | Explicit terminal outcome |

Every graph has a finite terminal path. Cycles for revisit content must be bounded by one-shot receipts or a defined repeat policy. The scenario browser can validate structural references, but runtime consumers still need to validate the authoritative action.

### Field 03 expansion — example graph skeletons

**Coldwater graph:** observe the two reports; select a water source to inspect; decide whether to set a temporary limit; resolve the water owner action; optionally reconcile the dated measurements; return after a day; record whether the shared rule was followed; close as verified, restricted, or unresolved. Missing the inspection leaves a safe defer path.

**Relay graph:** receive a dated signal; inspect its source; compare it with the recovered note; request service or preserve a restricted schedule; receive a communications result; optionally speak with the custodian; decide who may request a reply; deliver a verified response or close the signal as unverified. The graph does not create a second message store.

**Clinic graph:** review the request; confirm the receiving site; check team and route readiness; ask what action may be offered; dispatch or decline; receive the medical and expedition results; optionally plan a return; close with completed care, declined care, missed window, or unresolved request. All care action outcomes remain with the medical owner.

### Field 04 expansion — profile story branches

| Profile | Early beat | Midpoint complication | Commitment | Callback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coldwater | Two measurements disagree | A delivery claim changes expected demand | Choose a limit or delay | Verify actual draw |
| Relay | A signal uses an old call sign | The sender asks to keep one detail private | Set an access rule | Receive or refuse a follow-up |
| Clinic | A named request lacks a clear contact | The patient prefers another form of help | Dispatch, adapt, or decline | Confirm whether agreed help arrived |
| Kilowatt | A gauge flickers during a stable reading | One service reports a separate supply need | Inspect, reduce, or defer | Compare after-load reading |
| North Watch | Two rosters list the same shift differently | A reliable witness did not keep written notes | Reconcile or preserve dispute | Check the next handoff |
| Grain | Warning has an incomplete date | A trader offers stock from another source | Inspect, hold, or seek alternate supply | Review whether caution prevented loss |

Each arc has at least two valid outcomes and a branch that leaves one fact uncertain. Neither uncertainty nor refusal is treated as a failed story. Later prose references the selected outcome without claiming that a character endorses it.

### Field 05 expansion — profile side-quest workbook

The 24 optional tasks can be specified in greater detail:

| Profile | Task | Action and follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| Coldwater | Mark the old water line | Verify two physical references, then inspect the source |
| Coldwater | Find the missing ration note | Compare dates, then record the supported allocation |
| Coldwater | Return the borrowed container | Reconcile custody and report whether it is reusable |
| Coldwater | Ask the lower camp | Confirm its request and permit a later callback |
| Relay | Match the signal clock | Inspect timestamps before replying |
| Relay | Recover the local key list | Ask the custodian which entries remain valid |
| Relay | Replace the entry notice | Use a verified schedule and share-access rule |
| Relay | Deliver a corrected reply | Confirm recipient and record delivery outcome |
| Clinic | Find the named requester | Verify contact without exposing private detail |
| Clinic | Return the unopened case | Reconcile inventory and report what was not used |
| Clinic | Ask about a nearer meeting point | Confirm access through its owner |
| Clinic | Record the declined option | Preserve the actual choice and retry condition |
| Kilowatt | Read the maintenance slip | Compare its date with the current fault |
| Kilowatt | Check a second load | Query the existing power owner for another result |
| Kilowatt | Source a compatible component | Verify the item through current catalogs |
| Kilowatt | Post the operating limit | Publish only the supported service rule |
| North Watch | Interview the outgoing guard | Record the shift as a witnessed fact |
| North Watch | Reconcile the key return | Check custody before assigning a new holder |
| North Watch | Find a missing duty note | Keep the author/source attached to the record |
| North Watch | Review the next handoff | Confirm whether the new process was followed |
| Grain | Inspect the original label | Preserve provenance and uncertainty |
| Grain | Move one sealed crate | Reconcile location and custody |
| Grain | Ask the recipient about delay | Share the actual inspection state |
| Grain | Return after disposition | Confirm what the food owner accepted |

### Field 06 expansion — integration evidence matrix

The scenario designer creates a row for every objective node with current owner, input contract, output receipt, persistence owner, host observer, data reference, and existing coverage. Nodes that only expose a current owner action can be content integrations. Nodes that require a new initializer, new save identity, or new objective lifecycle need an explicit architecture and ownership decision.

Review recent accepted systems that may make a profile possible, including communications, colony/outpost, disaster response, education, archive, cartography, trade, seasonal conditions, and difficulty. These systems are dependencies to verify, not invitations to clone. Mark profiles that rely on active XP work or any current integration batch as deferred until the owner closes the relevant claim.

### Field 07 expansion — scenario browser detail contract

The browser card uses consistent facts: title, premise, starting pressure, first decision, objective count by type, dependency readiness, and save behavior. The detail screen can show the opening briefing, current evidence known at start, supported settings, and the kinds of callbacks expected. It does not show a numeric rating unsupported by design evidence.

The player can return from confirmation to details without losing selection. A failed profile validation lists the missing row and the owning catalog in plain text. A newly disabled profile stays visible with a reason only if the current UI route has a meaningful way to explain that status; otherwise it is hidden from new starts while existing saves remain loadable.

### Field 08 expansion — accessibility and commitment clarity

Before starting, communicate whether the profile uses tutorial guidance, changes the expected campaign start, or introduces a time-sensitive first request. The player can inspect conditions in text and compare profile pressures without relying on icon color. Long opening briefings need headings, short paragraphs, and an accessible scroll region with the start control reachable.

During play, the objective view distinguishes required, optional, completed, failed, canceled, and unresolved. A canceled node should tell the player whether another path exists. Keyboard focus returns to the selected node after a receipt arrives. Reduced motion and sound settings continue to come from the existing preference owner.

### Field 09 expansion — graph size, restart, and versioning

Profile tests should include 1, 6, 12, and 24 profiles with graphs containing 8, 20, and 40 nodes, both valid and intentionally invalid references. Measure validation, preview, start initialization, first save, resume, and cancellation. Reject cyclic graphs without a repeat rule and nonterminal graphs with no resolution path.

Restart creates a new campaign identity according to the existing save contract; it does not reset the active campaign in place. Load resumes the selected revision and objective receipts. Updating profile content must not rewrite an active run’s graph silently. Record profile version alongside any current campaign metadata that the approved save owner can hold.

### Field 10 expansion — authoring and integration handoff

The design handoff includes six objective graph skeletons, the 24 side-task workbook, profile manifest proposals, integration evidence rows, opening and closing prose, and UI screenshots or text wireframes. It also includes a negative-content list: no duplicate condition tracks, no local versions of inventory or difficulty, no unsupported treatments, no hidden morality score, and no direct mutation of another system’s private state.

The first package can be delivered entirely through existing quest and campaign surfaces if those surfaces can represent a distinct starting profile. If a missing launch contract remains, the foreman receives an architecture proposal with one profile example, rollback case, and save owner request. The remaining profiles stay authored as disabled content until that seam is accepted.

## Pass 6 — Six-profile campaign anthology and start-state matrix

### Field 01 expansion — campaign variety through controlled premises

The anthology should cover six kinds of player attention: verify a measurement, trace a message, arrange a visit, protect a service, reconcile work records, and judge an uncertain stock report. The player sees the type of play in the scenario browser and can choose a different profile when they want a different opening. All six remain within the same survival campaign rules, item authority, map, survivor roster, and save contract.

Keep the amount of starting state small enough to explain. Each profile introduces one dominant pressure and at most two supporting pressures. Supporting conditions deepen the decision but cannot require an undocumented system. A profile that starts with three unrelated emergencies is not difficult in a useful way; it is simply unclear.

### Field 02 expansion — start bundle dependency order

The start bundle resolves data in a fixed order:

1. Validate the profile and requested revision.
2. Validate every referenced location, character, item, message, and objective.
3. Check existing campaign and save-slot eligibility.
4. Request owner-supported starting facts in the documented order.
5. Collect successful initialization receipts.
6. Establish the first objective and its source.
7. Activate the campaign identity.
8. Show the resulting initial state before the player commits to advancing time.

Each stage has a compensating action or a hard failure before activation. If an owner has already committed state and cannot roll it back, its initialization API is not ready for this bundle. The scenario must not mask a partial start by displaying the browser again.

### Field 03 expansion — opening bundles for all six profiles

| Profile | Opening bundle | First board card | First result to observe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coldwater | Two dated source reports and one mapped water point | Inspect, set a provisional limit, or ask for evidence | Current water/access result |
| Relay | One received signal, old service note, and custodian contact | Verify sender, test relay, or set a restricted reply rule | Communications receipt |
| Clinic | A request, a permitted contact route, and a receiving site | Clarify, prepare, dispatch, or close | Medical/expedition result |
| Kilowatt | Existing power service with one recorded fault | Inspect, reduce a supported load, or defer | Power owner status |
| North Watch | Two duty records and one reachable outpost | Inspect, reconcile, or leave the shift unresolved | Duty/outpost receipt |
| Grain | One sealed stock lot and a dated warning | Hold, inspect, or seek another source | Food/inventory disposition |

These bundles do not introduce new residents or item definitions by implication. The content audit must match proposed references to current catalogs before a profile is enabled.

### Field 04 expansion — scenario beat books

**Coldwater:** the first report gives a level without a date; the second is dated but measured from a different point. A local contact offers an old allocation rule. The player can verify the point, choose a conservative temporary limit, or delay commitment. A later delivery receipt challenges whether the limit was followed. The closeout can be confirmed, disputed, or unresolved.

**Relay:** the received signal uses a retired call sign. A physical note suggests who sent it, but its date is damaged. The custodian offers limited service if the player preserves local access hours. The player can verify, reply with a caveat, or refuse to relay a private detail. A later signal reveals whether the access rule works for the sender.

**Clinic:** the first request is short and lacks a specific action. The receiving site confirms a time window but asks that one personal detail stay private. The player can gather more information, prepare a team, or close the request. Route delay and recipient refusal remain distinct. A return visit shows only what the person allowed to be shared.

**Kilowatt:** a gauge flickers while a device continues to run. A maintenance slip was recorded after the last power event, but the load has since changed. The player can inspect, reduce an owner-supported load, or defer. A second observation tests whether the first repair resolved the fault.

**North Watch:** the roster shows two names for one duty and no signature for the handoff. The outgoing guard can describe the shift but cannot certify the next one. The player may inspect current presence, ask the outpost owner to reconcile, or leave the record disputed. A later handoff shows whether the new method provides better evidence.

**Grain:** a warning label lacks its revision date. A sealed lot can be held while the player checks provenance or finds an alternate source. The player chooses whether to keep the stock unavailable, move it through an accepted storage path, or seek a food-owner disposition. The callback confirms the actual cost of the hold or the result of the inspection.

### Field 05 expansion — objective-to-outcome mapping

Every primary objective should provide three outputs: a gameplay result from the current owner; an information result that clarifies or preserves a fact; and a narrative result showing who noticed the decision. Optional objectives may improve information or logistics but cannot add a hidden score that silently changes the primary result.

| Objective family | Primary result | Optional contribution | Valid unresolved ending |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Owner-accepted inspection or source record | Second witness or document | Conflicting sources remain |
| Logistics | Accepted reservation, route, or transfer | Alternate delivery plan | Delivery remains unavailable |
| Access | Authorized visit or service rule | Local contact and notice | Permission remains pending |
| Service | Existing service state changes | Follow-up inspection | Service stays restricted |
| Record | Current history owner accepts correction | Provenance or witness note | Dispute is preserved |
| Recovery | Return, repair, or safe closeout | Site callback | Work remains incomplete |

### Field 06 expansion — owner portfolio for anthology content

Make an owner portfolio before requesting a scenario framework. The water scenario reads the current water service and inventory owners. The relay scenario reads the communication and power owners. The clinic scenario reads medical, expedition, and inventory. The Kilowatt scenario reads power and maintenance/part catalogs. North Watch reads outpost and duty/relationship records. Grain reads food preservation and inventory. Each row needs a current API and persistence reference before it can move beyond draft.

The portfolio compares these starts with currently integrated work on communications, outposts and colonies, disaster response, seasonal conditions, cartography, archives, education, trade, and difficulty. A scenario may compose those systems, but it cannot create a parallel operator for them. If an accepted plan already owns a start profile or campaign route, send the relevant scene and objective cards to that owner.

### Field 07 expansion — scenario selection state map

The browser progresses through list, profile detail, settings review, slot selection, validation, confirmation, initialization, and first objective. Back navigation between the first three stages cannot mutate the campaign. A failure during validation identifies the broken reference. A failure during initialization displays whether the previous campaign remains intact and whether a retry is safe.

The player can compare two profiles side by side. The comparison fields are opening uncertainty, first action, core owner systems, time pressure, optional goal shape, accessibility behavior, and measured time band when available. A simple tag such as “medical” or “power” is not enough to distinguish profiles.

### Field 08 expansion — onboarding and fair failure

Teach only the first action needed for the selected profile. The prompt describes the current interface and the actual command. It does not reveal the correct answer. Players can dismiss or revisit guidance through the existing tutorial preferences.

Every primary objective has at least one recoverable route or one plainly stated terminal condition. If a player misses a time window, the scenario says what changed and whether there is another way forward. Optional objectives may expire, but their expiry is visible when the choice is still actionable. Failure to perform an optional task does not retroactively make the scenario a loss.

### Field 09 expansion — version and content compatibility cases

Test new starts and active saves under: matching profile revision; profile content updated after the save; profile no longer offered for new starts; missing optional objective; and invalid required owner reference. Active campaigns must preserve their selected profile revision or follow an explicit migration. Invalid new content is blocked from starting without corrupting current saves.

The performance matrix measures browser open, comparison, detail loading, validation, initialization, first save, and resumed load with 1, 6, 12, and 24 profiles. Measure objective graph evaluation for both short and long graphs. Keep full story text out of repeated campaign ticks unless a current content system requires otherwise.

### Field 10 expansion — anthology sign-off packet

The final packet contains a one-page anthology map, six setup bundles, objective graphs, 24 optional tasks, all owner references, start rollback behavior, sample opening and ending text, browser flow, compatibility cases, and the evidence that each profile is distinct. It lists data rows that exist, rows that require content additions, and rows blocked on architecture.

The first profile is accepted only after cancellation leaves no partial state, initialization creates one complete run, save/load retains the profile and objective receipts, and the first result is visible through the appropriate owner surface. Further profiles expand only after this contract is proven and the live integration ledger allows their dependencies.

## Pass 6 — Scenario episode scripts and validation workbook

### Field 01 expansion — what makes a profile mechanically distinct

Profiles can share a system and still feel different when their first evidence, decision timing, and follow-up differ. The distinction test compares six moments: opening information, first action, first scarce commitment, first external owner result, midpoint complication, and ending callback. Two profiles that differ only in opening prose fail the test. Two profiles that share an owner can remain separate when one asks the player to verify evidence and the other asks them to preserve access.

Profile scope should stay small enough for a clear debrief. A run can include one primary goal, two supporting systems, and several optional objectives. If the profile depends on a second major campaign system, make it an optional bridge objective or defer the profile until the dependency is available.

### Field 02 expansion — validation result vocabulary

The start validator should return a bounded result category and a reference the UI can explain:

| Category | Example cause | Safe response |
|---|---|---|
| Ready | All required references and owner calls are valid | Continue to confirmation |
| Missing content | Required item, person, or place ID absent | Disable the start and identify the catalog |
| Stale profile | Requested revision is unavailable | Offer current profiles without changing a save |
| Owner rejected | Initial fact is not accepted by its owner | Report the owner reason and stop activation |
| Save conflict | Target slot is occupied or unavailable | Return to slot selection |
| Incompatible setting | Selected option is unsupported | Show supported options and preserve preferences |
| Rollback incomplete | An owner cannot undo a staged mutation | Treat the initializer as not ready |

The UI cannot reinterpret a rejected owner response as success. All required validation finishes before the final confirmation wherever possible.

### Field 03 expansion — profile state cards

| Profile | Starting facts | First two objectives | Initial exclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coldwater | Mapped source; dated and undated reports | Verify source; inspect owner-supported limit | No fire or clinic dependency |
| Relay | Existing relay; signal with old call sign | Trace source; request limited service | No standalone radio subsystem |
| Clinic | Request source; receiving site; travel window | Confirm contact; prepare dispatch | No new disease or patient store |
| Kilowatt | Existing power issue; maintenance slip | Inspect fault; select supported load action | No local power counter |
| North Watch | Current outpost; conflicting duty notes | Verify people present; reconcile assignment | No second settlement roster |
| Grain | Existing stock; uncertain warning | Check provenance; ask for owner disposition | No duplicate food shelf-life state |

These exclusions are useful authoring constraints. They stop optional campaign profiles from quietly acquiring parallel gameplay state during content production.

### Field 04 expansion — five-scene scripts

Every profile can use a five-scene structure while varying the actual content:

| Scene | Coldwater | Relay | Clinic | Kilowatt | North Watch | Grain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arrival | Two source marks disagree | Signal arrives under an old name | Request lacks an action | Gauge disagrees with work note | Roster has a blank shift | Label date is missing |
| First inquiry | Find who measured | Ask who recognizes the call sign | Confirm who wants contact | Read the service history | Ask who saw the handoff | Trace the supplier stamp |
| Complication | Use point differs from map | Custodian requests limited access | Recipient changes the contact boundary | Another owner reports a separate load | Witness remembers the shift differently | Alternate stock is not yet available |
| Commitment | Set limit or defer | Reply, restrict, or wait | Dispatch, adapt, or decline | Inspect, reduce, or defer | Reconcile or preserve dispute | Hold, inspect, or seek another source |
| Return | Compare actual draw | Check for a new verified signal | Review agreed contact | Check the new reading | Confirm the next handoff | Reveal actual stock disposition |

The scenes are templates for authored implementation. They need named locations, canonical speakers, quest triggers, dialog keys, and owner receipts before they become data.

### Field 05 expansion — optional objective result states

Each profile’s optional objectives can end in one of four result states: completed and verified; completed with a dispute; expired because the relevant window passed; or explicitly declined. A result state includes a short debrief line and a future callback condition when appropriate. None is translated to a hidden score.

For content volume, each profile should eventually contain one investigation objective, one logistics objective, one access/relationship objective, one recovery objective, and two short optional conversations. That gives a target of 36 distinct optional units across six profiles. A unit is distinct only when its player action, source, or result changes; a renamed copy does not count.

### Field 06 expansion — existing owner and plan audit map

For every profile, compare proposed setup and objectives against the current campaign, quest, difficulty, inventory, map, and save contracts. Where a profile uses communications, verify the current communication catalog and event consumers. Where it uses an outpost, verify the current outpost and colony owners. Where it uses seasonal or emergency conditions, check the corresponding live owner and accepted plan. Where it references archives or education, verify that the existing data consumers and routes still exist.

Record the audit date and evidence location. If a current plan owns a matching profile, the scenario work is a candidate integration contribution, not a second implementation claim. The current ledger remains authoritative if an older index disagrees.

### Field 07 expansion — debrief and restart surface

The debrief begins with the primary objective state, then lists optional objectives, owner-confirmed outcomes, unresolved facts, and callbacks. It avoids a single campaign score. The player can open the canonical owner panel from each result or return to the campaign. If an objective was unavailable because of a disabled dependency, the debrief says so rather than calling it failed.

Restart reopens the profile detail and asks for an eligible save slot under the current contract. It summarizes what a new run initializes and whether the former run remains available. There is no generic “retry” button that may overwrite the active campaign.

### Field 08 expansion — challenge explanation and accessible onboarding

Scenario pressure labels need an explanation of the actual constraint: a route window, an uncertain report, a limited stock, a work shift, or an access agreement. They are not subjective difficulty grades. The scenario offers a clear first step and a safe way to request more information.

Tutorial text is split into short prompts tied to commands. Screen readers and keyboard/controller navigation can reach the objective graph, and graph edges have text labels. Color and line shape are redundant aids. A long objective list can collapse completed optional work while retaining a count and read-only details.

### Field 09 expansion — migration and disabled-profile behavior

Maintain separate compatibility notes for profile content, objective graph, and campaign save version. Removing a profile from new starts does not delete a run already in progress. A change to wording can be applied through localization/content revision; a change to objective behavior requires an explicit migration or pinned revision. Missing optional rows can be marked unavailable; missing required rows block load only through a save migration decision.

Profile validation should be deterministic, bounded by referenced rows, and independent of browser open frequency. Measure initialization and restore with long objective history and several completed profiles. New profile availability should be driven by a validated catalog, not a stale UI cache.

### Field 10 expansion — authored scenario package contents

For each profile, prepare a manifest draft, five-scene script, primary graph, six optional objective outlines, branch table, owner audit map, start and restart screenshots or wireframe, accessibility review, save behavior, and invalid-start examples. Review each artifact as evidence for a playable contract, not as a word-count target.

The content director can approve a profile as narrative-ready while the integration owner keeps it disabled. A profile becomes an implementation candidate only when the start path can call current owners, the save owner can preserve identity, and the first result is observable. If those conditions are not met, keep the script useful to existing quest surfaces and defer the scenario browser change.

## Pass 7 — Scenario production dossiers and playthrough coverage

### Field 01 expansion — profile pressure and decision density

Each scenario should create at least three meaningful decisions: a first information decision, a mid-run commitment, and an ending or deferral decision. A meaningful decision has two or more valid actions, a cost or uncertainty the player can understand, and a result that changes an owner fact or a future piece of information. More branches are not automatically better if the player cannot distinguish them.

Profile pressure is expressed through concrete facts. Coldwater has a measurement discrepancy and a shared-use question. Relay has uncertain provenance and an access boundary. Clinic has request ambiguity and travel commitment. Kilowatt has a fault report and supported load options. North Watch has incompatible records and an unverified handoff. Grain has uncertain warning provenance and stock availability. Do not add unbounded emergencies to make one profile feel more difficult.

### Field 02 expansion — canonical start profile data sheet

| Data field | Review question |
|---|---|
| Profile identity | Is the ID unique and stable across revisions? |
| Required references | Do all locations, items, characters, and objective nodes exist? |
| Owner initializers | Does each start fact use an existing supported command? |
| Initial evidence | Is each report sourced, dated, and given confidence wording? |
| Objective root | Can the first node be reached immediately? |
| Alternate start | What happens if a required reference is unavailable? |
| Accessibility | Does the profile use supported input and display settings? |
| Save identity | Which current owner stores the profile and revision? |
| Rollback | Can all staged owner mutations be undone before activation? |
| Closeout | Which owner result ends the primary objective? |
| Callback | What receipt enables the later scene? |
| Content version | How does an active save retain its authored revision? |

### Field 03 expansion — candidate objective node inventories

| Profile | Candidate node IDs | Owner evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Coldwater | coldwater_read_reports, inspect_source, choose_limit, review_draw | Water/map/quest receipts |
| Relay | relay_open_signal, verify_call_sign, choose_access, deliver_reply | Communications/access receipt |
| Clinic | clinic_review_request, verify_contact, prepare_route, close_visit | Medical/expedition receipt |
| Kilowatt | kilowatt_read_fault, inspect_load, choose_action, recheck_service | Power/service receipt |
| North Watch | watch_compare_rosters, verify_presence, request_reconcile, inspect_handoff | Duty/outpost receipt |
| Grain | grain_read_warning, inspect_provenance, select_disposition, revisit_stock | Food/inventory receipt |

Each node ID is provisional. A production node references a public current quest or owner command and has both a success and a no-result outcome. If the owner provides no API for the claimed evidence, the node stays a content proposal.

### Field 04 expansion — distinct opening and ending sequences

**Coldwater opening:** the player receives one measured value without a date and one dated value from another landmark. A local contact explains that the old allocation rule may still be in use. The player can verify, set a supported temporary condition, or postpone. The ending reports either a confirmed water-owner state or an unresolved allocation, then schedules a return only if the current system permits it.

**Relay opening:** an incoming signal uses an old call sign. The player can compare its timestamp, ask the custodian, or test available service. The sender may be identifiable while one piece of content remains private. The ending records whether a reply was sent, restricted, or withheld.

**Clinic opening:** a direct request has no clear care action, and the receiving site’s visit window is limited. The player can ask what is wanted, arrange a team, or decline the visit. The ending displays the actual travel and medical receipts with the contact boundary.

**Kilowatt opening:** a gauge reading does not match a maintenance note. The player can inspect the load, reduce a supported service, or wait for a specialist. The ending states whether the owner reports normal, limited, or unresolved service.

**North Watch opening:** the roster records a shift that the current witness remembers differently. The player can inspect who is present, request reconciliation, or preserve the record dispute. The ending names which assignment was confirmed and which record remains uncertain.

**Grain opening:** the warning label lacks a clear revision. The player can hold the stock, trace its source, or find a supported alternative. The ending reports the disposition accepted by the food owner and the actual cost of waiting.

### Field 05 expansion — branching side-task cards

| Candidate task | Branch A | Branch B | Persistent result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compare the two Coldwater marks | Agree after inspection | Keep dispute open | Source confidence and follow-up |
| Ask who heard the relay | Share a verified answer | Withhold a private detail | Message provenance |
| Offer a clinic time | Recipient accepts | Recipient declines | Visit or refusal receipt |
| Inspect the maintenance slip | Fault matches | Date or load differs | Power review state |
| Check the night roster | Person is present | Presence remains unknown | Duty evidence |
| Read the stock warning | Source is current | Revision cannot be found | Food-owner inspection |
| Return the borrowed scale | Custodian accepts it | Custody remains disputed | Inventory/quest result |
| Request a second source | Another source responds | No source available | Evidence status |
| Ask for access hours | Shared window agreed | Permission deferred | Location-access result |
| Deliver a corrected notice | Notice accepted | Owner requires review | Current notice state |
| Recheck the site tomorrow | Condition changed | No new observation | One-shot callback |
